key_insight: The paper gives provable classical and quantum methods to find the Slater determinant with maximum fidelity to a fermionic many-body state, showing a sharp optimization transition at fidelity 2/3.
engineering_relevance: This enables more compact and interpretable fermionic state approximations for quantum simulation, Hartree-Fock-style initialization, and agnostic tomography with polynomial resource guarantees in relevant parameters.
method: Classical and quantum algorithms search over Slater determinants and return one within ε of the optimal fidelity.
With quantum-state copies, the method uses poly(m,n,1/ε) samples of ρ.
The analysis also characterizes the landscape: above 2/3 fidelity stationary points are globally optimal, while below 2/3 spurious stationary points can appear.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical performance guarantees, matching hardness lower bounds under standard conjectures, and an application to Fermi-Hubbard states extracted from neural quantum state solutions.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees are parameterized and complexity-theoretic; practical performance may depend on state preparation cost, optimization stability, and how closely real systems match the assumed fermionic model.
